subject: Throughput & concurrency recap — FastCart traffic profile validation
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fastcart.com>, Tom Fletcher <tom.fletcher@fastcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — throughput & streaming profile (actions attached)

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and the asks so we can size a brief technical POC. Attaching the load profile CSV and a draft mutual action plan.

Summary from our call:
- Business goal: inline recommendation + personalized summaries in checkout; target 95th latency <= 250ms for non-streaming completions and tail <= 500ms for streaming sessions (95th token latency).
- Traffic shape: baseline QPS ~12 req/s, expected steady tokens per request ~1.2k (generation+context), peak 2x baseline during 16:00–17:30 PST window; peak sessions are largely streaming (~60% of peak requests).
- Concurrency: concurrent active streams at peak estimated ~45 simultaneous sessions, steady-state concurrent non-streaming workers ~12.
- Cost/availability constraints: prefer a single-region footprint in us-west with the option to fail over to us-east in emergencies.

Asks / next steps:
1) Could you confirm the percent of requests that include large context (>=3k tokens)? We had it at ~10%.
2) Share a sanitized sample request/response (just sizes) so we can validate prefix caching impact.
3) Approve the POC scope in the attached MAP (2-week POC: ingest sample traffic, run a throughput bench, validate streaming latency SLOs).

Preliminary Redwood sizing notes (high level) — we will flesh these internally and validate on the POC:
- Sustained throughput target: ~12 QPS * 1.2k tokens ~ 14.4k tokens/sec steady; peak token velocity during the 90min window ~28.8k tokens/sec.
- Streaming sessions: need lower per-token tail latency, so we'll exercise smaller batch windows + KV cache warmers.

Attachments: fastcart_load_profile_v1.csv, mutual_action_plan_fastcart_v2.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up to walk the MAP and confirm scope.

—Priyom
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai

From: Elena Rossi <elena@fastcart.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Fletcher <tom.fletcher@fastcart.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 17:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — throughput & streaming profile (actions attached)

Thanks Priyom — this is great and matches our notes. Quick clarifications: 
- Large-context requests (~>=3k tokens) are closer to 8–12% (we saw recent growth after our catalogue expansion).
- Typical request sizes (sanitized average): context 700 tokens + response 500 tokens = ~1.2k total (matches your number).
- Peak multiplier: our traffic analysis shows a 1.8–2.2x multiplier for the 16:00–17:30 PST window; most of those are interactive streaming sessions from checkout assistants.

We can provide a sanitized sample payload (headers + token counts only) — I'll upload to the Drive folder by EOD. We'd like the POC to include:
- A streaming latency run capturing 95th token latency under injected background load,
- A verification of caching effect when the same customer context is repeated within a 10-minute window.

Tom and I are good with the MAP scope; please include an optional quantized fallback plan for cost control in the POC.

—Elena
Head of Product, FastCart
elena@fastcart.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FastCart quick capacity sketch + ops asks

Internal notes after reading Elena's reply + the load CSV: putting a quick back-of-envelope here so we have a working set for the tech deep-dive. Feel free to paste/copy into the POC plan.

Assumptions from CSV:
- Baseline QPS: 12 (matches); avg tokens/req 1.2k; peak multiplier 2.0; peak window 90 minutes; streaming fraction @peak = 0.60; large-context fraction = 0.10.

Token velocity estimates:
- Steady tokens/sec = 12 * 1200 = 14,400 t/s.
- Peak tokens/sec = 24 * 1200 = 28,800 t/s (for the 90min window).
- Streaming-specific token tail load: 0.6 * 28,800 = 17,280 t/s that needs low tail latency treatment.

Concurrency implications (very rough):
- If average streaming session emits tokens at ~20 t/s (typical for short-turn interactions), 17,280 t/s implies ~860 active streaming token emitters — that number seems high compared to Elena's 45 sessions estimate, so we need to confirm token-per-second-per-session. If instead sessions are bursty (200 t/s for 2–3s), the #sessions drops dramatically. Request Elena's instrumentation for tokens/sec per active stream.

Operational recommendations for POC:
1) Bootstrapped KV cache warmers for repeated context to reduce model work for 10% large-context cases.
2) Use continuous small batching for streaming to avoid adding token latency while still consolidating GPU work.
3) Exercise a quantized variant for background/non-critical requests to maintain cost envelope; keep fp16 for streaming-critical paths.
4) Pre-provision a small burst pool for the 90min window and validate autoscale cooldowns.

Next steps:
- Priyom: confirm with Elena tokens/sec per streaming session and upload sanitized sample payloads.
- Lauren: prepare readiness checklist for POC infra (network/whitelisting, KMS access).
- I'll draft a first-pass capacity runbook and bench plan by Wed EOD.

-Karthik
Director, Performance Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fastcart.com>, Tom Fletcher <tom.fletcher@fastcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — throughput & streaming profile (actions attached)

Elena — thanks, and appreciate the quick turn on the sample payloads. We've scheduled a 60-minute technical deep-dive to align on tokens/sec per-session and the exact traffic TTL for cache warmers. Invite attached (tech-dd-invite.ics).

Agenda (brief):
- Review sanitized sample sizes and per-session token emission rate (5–10 mins)
- Confirm peak window characteristics and concurrency math (10 mins)
- Bench plan: streaming latency capture & cache effectiveness (25 mins)
- Success criteria and MAP sign-off (10 mins)

If you prefer to share instrumentation ahead of the call, we can pre-run a micro-bench and bring initial numbers. Otherwise we'll capture live during the POC.

See you on the call — Priyom
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
